market_context: U.S. equities are undergoing a broad risk-off session led by technology and AI shares: QQQ is down 3.20%, NVDA 6.42%, and VIX has jumped 31.64% to 34.70. Reports cite tariff concerns, an ongoing AI-stock selloff, and uncertainty ahead of inflation-sensitive data including core PCE, jobless claims, durable-goods orders, and the GDP estimate; Treasury yields have been volatile while investors seek safety.

predictions.reasoning: SPY has already absorbed a sharp 2.19% decline and traded up from its early low of $695.45 to above $703, suggesting some intraday stabilization. The broader selloff and elevated VIX limit conviction, but oversold conditions and bond-market safety demand could support a modest late-session rebound.

Technology remains the session's weakest major segment, with QQQ down 3.20%, its five-day loss at 6.3%, and reports describing an accelerating AI-chip selloff ahead of inflation data. Nasdaq futures were reported down roughly 2.3% overnight, while NVDA and other AI-linked shares remain under pressure, favoring additional weakness into the close.

NVDA is down 6.42% and trading close to its $141.17 intraday low as the reported AI-chip liquidation intensifies; reports also identify Nvidia as the leader of the technology selloff. With volatility elevated and risk reduction concentrated in semiconductors, a retest of the low is more likely than a full recovery.

Bitcoin has fallen 2.75% to about $58105, after losing the psychologically important $60000 level, while the equity-market risk-off move and VIX above 34 indicate unfavorable near-term risk appetite. Crypto-specific reporting also describes bitcoin slipping as Nasdaq futures fell and volatility rose, supporting a modest continuation lower.
